hero.title: SNOMED CT in the European Health Data Space
hero.subtitle: Interactive demonstrators built from the EHDS implementation guides. See how SNOMED CT terminology bindings turn specifications into working, conformant FHIR data.

about.title: What is the EHDS?
about.body: The European Health Data Space is an EU Regulation (2025/327), directly applicable in every Member State. It creates a common framework for using electronic health data across Europe.

primary.title: Primary use
primary.body: People access, control and share their health data across borders for their own care.

secondary.title: Secondary use
secondary.body: Secure, trustworthy reuse of health data for research, innovation and policy-making.

market.title: Single market for EHR systems
market.body: Interoperability becomes a demonstrable, enforceable requirement for EHR products.

timeline.title: Key milestones
timeline.priorityCategories: Patient summary, ePrescription/eDispensation and secondary use

eehrxf.title: A common exchange format
eehrxf.body: Primary use relies on the European Electronic Health Record exchange Format (EEHRxF) and its priority data categories. Each category has a dataset specification whose terminology bindings frequently name SNOMED CT and LOINC as preferred code systems.
eehrxf.disclaimer: The dataset specifications are drafts prepared by Xt-EHR and are not yet final implementing acts.

ig.title: Computable implementation guides
ig.body: FHIR implementation guides, such as HL7 Europe's Patient Summary, are published as machine-readable packages. A package contains profiles that constrain FHIR resources, value sets, terminology bindings and examples, so software can read the specification directly instead of re-typing it from a document.

bindings.title: Terminology bindings with SNOMED CT
bindings.body: A binding links a coded element, such as a diagnosis, an allergen or a vaccine, to the value set its codes must come from, with a strength: required, extensible, preferred or example. SNOMED CT value sets are typically defined with ECL, which keeps them precise and current.
bindings.note: For EHR vendors this means terminology capability, not just message formats.

chain.title: From requirement to code
chain.body: Every coded field depends on a chain of specifications. Each layer refines the one before it, from what the EHDS requires down to the codes a system actually sends.

profile.title: FHIR profile
profile.source: HL7 Europe: how it is exchanged

valueSet.title: Value set binding
valueSet.source: IPS and MyHealth@EU: which codes are allowed

terminology.title: Terminology
terminology.source: SNOMED CT, searched live with ECL

chain.note: Comparing the layers reveals gaps. The Xt-EHR model lists Orphacode for rare diseases and ICD-O for cancer, but no EPS binding covers them yet. The EHDS badges in the demonstrators show which model each section realises.

build.title: How these demonstrators are built

read.title: Read the guide
read.body: Load the implementation guide's FHIR package and its profiles.

generate.title: Generate the forms
generate.body: Derive fields, cardinality and documentation from the profiles, focusing on the clinically relevant, SNOMED CT–coded elements.

bind.title: Bind the terminology
bind.body: Each coded field searches SNOMED CT live, constrained by its value set.

produce.title: Produce conformant FHIR
produce.body: Captured data is assembled into FHIR resources that claim the guide's profiles.

build.note: In every demonstrator, the FHIR and BINDING badges open the element definition and the value set straight from the guide.

patientSummary.title: EHDS Patient Summary
patientSummary.description: A spec-driven European Patient Summary: problems, allergies, medications, immunizations and more, assembled into a conformant EPS document.

laboratory.title: EHDS Laboratory Report
laboratory.description: Laboratory orders, specimens and results with SNOMED CT and LOINC, assembled into a FHIR DiagnosticReport.
